## v2.6.0 Release notes

This release introduces Toolbox with experimental Steam download node optimization, individual routing rule toggles, configurable match order, and automatic Wi-Fi connection at startup. It also refines the desktop interface and network diagnostics, with fixes for TUN address conflicts, DNS fallback, and routing priority.

### Toolbox and Steam download node optimization

- Added Toolbox to the sidebar, with Steam download node optimization as its first tool. It supports system proxy and TUN modes and is disabled by default.
- Discovers and validates Steam download candidates per outbound adapter, using bounded short tests and real download observations to gradually prefer better-performing nodes. Supports discovery across adapters, IPv4 and IPv6 candidates, and recognition of more Steam CDN hosts and redirect targets.
- Candidates must pass validation before trials and are continuously evaluated. Slow or failing nodes stop receiving new connections, while content mismatches revoke eligibility. Traffic, request, and concurrency limits keep probing from generating separate large-file speed tests.
- Added a dedicated detail page with candidate nodes, switched connections, actual download traffic, short-test reference rates, fallback counts, and diagnostics. Re-evaluate restarts learning.
- Separates client interruptions from upstream failures so interrupted downloads are not incorrectly counted as node failures. Connection switches and effective transfers are reported separately to show whether optimization is carrying download traffic.
- Toggle changes apply to new connections without actively interrupting existing downloads. Disabling cancels probes and clears rankings. Only supported Steam download hosts over TCP 80/443 are handled; system DNS, hosts, and Steam files are unchanged. HTTPS remains end-to-end encrypted without installing certificates.

### Routing rules

- Added an individual enable switch to each rule. Disabled rules remain in the list but are excluded from traffic matching and egress availability checks, with their status shown inline.
- Added configurable match order for process, domain, and IP rules, defaulting to process → domain → IP. The setting is saved even when the rule list is empty.
- Added a one-click action to disable rules referencing unavailable adapters, making it easier to recover after adapters are changed or disconnected. Rules can be re-enabled when needed.
- Routing backups now use format version 3 and preserve match order. Version 1 and 2 backups can still be imported, with type order derived from their existing priorities.
- Fixed broad adapter-specific IP rules taking precedence over DNS, process, and domain traffic in TUN mode. Refined third-party proxy exceptions so adapter rules do not override more specific non-adapter rules, while retaining live rule updates.
- Improved the rules toolbar, type tabs, and action layout for narrow windows.

### Desktop and interface

- Unified button, dropdown, and input borders, corners, and focus styles across light, dark, and frosted themes.
- Home now explicitly offers Maximum speed first and Schedule by weight. Clarified that weights control new-connection allocation, not bandwidth shares or rate limits; weight editing is disabled while running or degraded.
- Virtual adapters are hidden on Home by default, with a setting to show them. Improved detection of renamed virtual adapters and added hidden and selected counts while preserving existing selections.
- Improved alignment of the runtime status area and start button, reducing layout shifts as values change.
- Fixed inflated or erratic Home speed readings during frequent refreshes and improved throughput sampling stability.

### Network and startup

- Added Connect Wi-Fi at startup under Settings → Startup. Before automatic acceleration, selected wireless adapters try saved Windows networks that allow automatic connection and wait for connectivity within a bounded period.
- Fixed startup waits continuing with outdated settings. Disabling automatic startup, changing mode, or changing selected adapters cancels the pending attempt.
- TUN startup now checks interface subnets and selects an available address, addressing startup failures caused by the fixed address conflicting with Hyper-V, VPN, or other interfaces. Dual-stack and IPv4 fallback use the same selected address.
- Fixed DoH timeouts exhausting the fallback budget in automatic DNS mode, preserving time for subsequent DNS servers. Explicitly selected DoH providers retain their encrypted resolution policy.
- Improved startup preflight to retain completed diagnostic results when later checks time out or output is truncated. Extended the check window and report virtual adapters, IPv4 forwarding, and network sharing as environment information to reduce unnecessary risk prompts.
- Both system proxy and TUN startup check selected adapters for duplicate source IPs and identify the affected adapters and addresses before starting.

### Stability and maintenance

- Network diagnostics now preserve actual ICMP system errors instead of reporting local binding or API failures as 100% packet loss. Unavailable measurements display as “—”.
- Expanded support logs for automatic startup waits, Wi-Fi connection attempts, DNS validation, and TUN address selection. Windows Core builds now include the Git commit to identify the source revision.
- Improved DNS and health-check cache indexing to reduce frequent lookup and status-read overhead.
- Improved legacy configuration migration errors with the actual input file, conflicting ports, and repair examples.
- Added an upgrade check and repair tool under the repository's `tools/support` directory. It provides environment checks and confirmed repair cleanup for process locks, service state, and file writability while preserving user configuration and rules.
- Extended desktop–Core communication with Steam optimization configuration and capability detection, including recognition of unsupported older Core builds.
- Added regression coverage for Steam optimization, rule order, unavailable-rule disabling, startup Wi-Fi, TUN address selection, DNS fallback, and throughput sampling. Improved IPv6 test handling for unsupported environments.

### Upgrade notes

- Supports Windows 10/11 x64. Install the official signed package over an existing installation; the installer safely stops HypoMux and the independent Core service before replacing files.
- After upgrading, stop and restart aggregation/TUN once to apply the new routing configuration and TUN address selection. Re-saving rules alone does not update an older TUN main configuration.
- Steam download node optimization is experimental and disabled by default. Results depend on available CDN nodes and network conditions; faster downloads or full bandwidth are not guaranteed. Compare sustained download speeds for the same game and download region. The share of traffic carried by switched nodes is not a speed improvement percentage.
- Older routing backups can be imported into this release, but v2.5.9 cannot directly import format version 3 backups. If rollback is planned, export and retain a rule backup using the old version before upgrading.
- If an in-place upgrade is blocked, follow the instructions for the check and repair tool under the repository's `tools/support` directory, then run the official installer again.
- GitHub Releases and Tencent CNB Release continue to distribute the same SignPath-signed installer. Automatic updates still verify the Ed25519 manifest, file size, SHA-256, and Windows Authenticode signature.

> Thanks to SignPath.io for providing Windows code-signing services for HypoMux, and to SignPath Foundation for issuing the project's open-source code-signing certificate.
